# Phase 01.1 Plan 05: Design System Tracer Summary

**Newsreader/Instrument Sans/IBM Plex Mono self-hosted via next/font, a two-file Cena token layer wired through `globals.css` into every shadcn semantic role, Button re-skinned at a universal 44px floor, and three tripwires gating SC1 at both source and compiled output.**

## Performance

- **Duration:** 32 min
- **Started:** 2026-08-05T01:05:00Z
- **Completed:** 2026-08-05T01:37:00Z
- **Tasks:** 2
- **Files modified:** 8 (5 created, 3 modified)

## Accomplishments

- **One production-quality path wired through all six layers 01.1 touches** — font declaration → token file → `globals.css` entry point → primitive → shipped surface (login, which inherits the change and was deliberately not edited) → automated gate. Proven with a real build and the full suite, not asserted.
- **Three research unknowns killed on the tracer's budget rather than after ten committed layers** (see *Unknowns Resolved* below): Tailwind v4's handling of `@theme`-adjacent imports, the spacing/container collision risk, and whether the 44px floor is reachable in the primitive layer.
- **The Cena ramp is live as a value-level change.** `:root` declares no colour of its own — it maps every shadcn role onto a `--cena-*` token, which is why re-skinning 41 files becomes an edit to one file rather than a utility rewrite across the surface.
- **SC1 is gated at two independent layers** with a one-entry justified allowlist, and SC3's touch floor is gated at the token layer. All three tripwires were observed failing with offender-naming messages before being committed green.
- **The Phase 01 suite is untouched in meaning:** 641 baseline tests still pass, `tests/lib/theme-width-scale.test.ts` included.

## Task Commits

1. **Task 1: End-to-end "the login page renders in Cena's design"** — `3e1188a` (feat)
2. **Task 2: SC1 tripwires + the touch-floor gate** — `2bb0b7a` (test)

## Files Created/Modified

- `app/tokens/cena.css` *(new)* — the 16-token locked Cena product brand, values verbatim from UI-SPEC § Color. Carries the "three ink values, not four" rationale and a deliberately empty `.dark`.
- `app/tokens/primitives.css` *(new)* — brand-agnostic shape, motion, elevation, `--tracking-caps`. Header records why the spacing scale must stay in `globals.css` and which Tailwind names collide.
- `app/globals.css` — adds both token imports and `--font-serif`; maps all 30 semantic roles to `--cena-*`; adds `--destructive-foreground` and its `@theme inline` companion; serif base rule for `h1`–`h6`; both stale contract comments rewritten.
- `app/layout.tsx` — three `next/font/google` families replacing the single Inter call.
- `components/ui/button.tsx` — re-skinned; eight size variants raised to the floor; `min-h-11` in the cva base.
- `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` *(new)* — SC1 layer 1, source scan, one-entry allowlist.
- `tests/theme/build-assets.test.ts` *(new)* — SC1 layer 2, compiled-output scan.
- `tests/theme/touch-targets.test.ts` *(new)* — SC3's token-level half.

## Unknowns Resolved

The three the plan named as this tracer's reason for existing:

| Unknown | Verdict |
|---|---|
| **A1** — does Tailwind v4's PostCSS plugin process token files reached by `@import` from `globals.css`? | **Yes.** All 16 `--cena-*` tokens and all of `primitives.css` appear in `.next/static/chunks/*.css`, and `--background:var(--cena-paper)` resolves through to the utilities. The split is purely organisational, as research assumed. |
| **A2** — do the Cena spacing names collide with Tailwind's container scale? | **No new collision introduced.** The spacing scale was left byte-identical and no `--spacing-<k>` was added, so `theme-width-scale.test.ts` stays green and keeps its meaning. The risk was real but is now closed for this wave; it returns for any later wave that adds a spacing name. |
| **Open Question 6** — is the 44px floor achievable in the primitive layer? | **Yes, and it is now decided.** `min-h-11` in the cva base plus per-variant heights covers all eight sizes without touching a single surface. Verified `h-11` → `calc(var(--spacing) * 11)` with `--spacing: .25rem` = 44px in the compiled CSS. |

## Tripwire Failure Evidence

Each tripwire was deliberately broken, observed red, and reverted. `git diff` confirms no probe artifact survived.

**1. `no-third-party-assets.test.ts`** — added `app/tokens/__break-probe.css` containing a Google Fonts `@import`:

> `SC1 VIOLATION — 2 third-party asset request(s) not on the allowlist:`
> `  app/tokens/__break-probe.css:2  [CSS @import]  https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto&display=swap`
> `  app/tokens/__break-probe.css:2  [CSS url(...)]  https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto&display=swap`
> …*"If this is the design system's `tokens/fonts.css` … DO NOT ADD IT."*

Named the file, line, position kind and URL, and caught it in **both** asset positions.

**2. `build-assets.test.ts`** — appended an absolute `@import` to the compiled chunk:

> `SC1 VIOLATION — the compiled CSS asks the browser to fetch from an external origin:`
> `  .next/static/chunks/1tq9jtbfoidea.css  url(https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto)`

Two assertions went red (the `url()` check and the broader absolute-URL check). **Separately verified the missing-build path:** with `.next/static/chunks` renamed away, all five cases fail with *"…it FAILS rather than skipping — a build-output test that silently passes on a missing build proves nothing… Run `pnpm build` first"*. It does not skip.

**3. `touch-targets.test.ts`** — set the `sm` variant to `h-9`:

> `SC3 VIOLATION — Button size "sm" is 36px, below the 44px touch floor.`
> `  sm: "h-9 gap-1.5 rounded-… px-3 … [&_svg:not([class*='size-'])]:size-3.5"`

*(The elided radius is written `rounded-…` rather than with square brackets:
bracketed elisions in prose are what code review CR-01 traced the total outage
to, back when Tailwind scanned this directory as source.)*

Named the variant, converted units to pixels, and **correctly read `h-9` as the control box while ignoring the `size-3.5` svg glyph override in the same string** — the false-positive the tokenised matcher exists to prevent.

## Decisions Made

1. **Buttons render at the Label role.** The plan said to keep "each variant's distinct … type size", but UI-SPEC's Typography table maps buttons to Label (14px/600) and permits exactly four roles and two weights. Keeping `text-xs` and the imported system's arbitrary 0.8rem size would have shipped six sizes. Resolved toward the contract: `text-label` on the base string, semantic distinction preserved via padding, gap and icon size. This also retired `font-medium` (500) — the only third weight in the product.
2. **Three imported token names renamed, not declared.** This file is imported *after* `tailwindcss`, so a `:root` declaration wins over Tailwind's own theme variable of the same name and silently redefines the utility that reads it — the same failure mode as the width-shield defect, one namespace over. `--radius-xs`, `--shadow-sm` and `--shadow-xl` all collide. They became `--radius-sheet`/`--radius-full`, `--shadow-raised` and `--shadow-overlay`, with the mapping recorded in the file header for the waves that re-implement the diner surface.
3. **`--radius-md` consumed, not shadowed.** `globals.css` already owns a calc-based `sm`..`4xl` radius scale derived from `--radius`; only the two shapes it has no name for were added.
4. **Shadows re-tinted, geometry unchanged.** The one sourced elevation fact is that Cena's shadows are tisza-tinted `rgba(54, 66, 65, …)` — cool green-grey, not the warm brown the imported README claims. Tailwind's geometry and alpha are kept verbatim so only the hue is new; nothing was invented.
5. **Reduced-motion zeroing added at the token layer** (`@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroing the durations) so every consumer inherits it rather than each component remembering. This is [Rule 2] territory — see Deviations.
6. **Charts mapped onto the ramp.** `--chart-1..5` had no Cena equivalent but were the last zinc/oklch greyscale values in the file; they became an accent→ink sequence so the "no zinc ramp value survives" truth holds literally. Nothing consumes them in v1.
7. **Comments are not excepted by the source scan.** A commented-out external asset cannot make a request, but it signals intent and is one uncomment from shipping — and writing a stripper is worse, because the naive version truncates at the `//` inside `https://`. Consequence: my own `app/layout.tsx` comment had to be reworded to stop naming the CDN URL literally. That is the tripwire working, and it is noted inline so the next author is not confused.

## Deviations from Plan

### Auto-fixed Issues

**1. [Rule 2 — Missing Critical] Added `--destructive-foreground` and its `@theme inline` mapping**
- **Found during:** Task 1 (step 3)
- **Issue:** The plan's load-bearing assignment list names `--destructive-foreground: var(--cena-paper)`, but the key does not exist in `:root` today and there is no `--color-destructive-foreground` in `@theme inline`. Declaring only the `:root` half would have produced a dead token that no utility can reach.
- **Fix:** Added both halves, so `text-destructive-foreground` / `bg-destructive-foreground` actually resolve.
- **Files modified:** `app/globals.css`
- **Verification:** `pnpm build` exit 0; token present in compiled CSS.
- **Committed in:** `3e1188a`

**2. [Rule 2 — Missing Critical] Reduced-motion zeroing in the motion tokens**
- **Found during:** Task 1 (step 2)
- **Issue:** The design system's own description includes "reduced-motion zeroing", and the plan asked for `--duration-*` tokens without one. Motion honouring a user's stated accessibility preference is a correctness requirement, not a feature.
- **Fix:** `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` zeroing `--duration-base` and `--duration-slow` at `:root`, so every consumer inherits it.
- **Files modified:** `app/tokens/primitives.css`
- **Verification:** Both `--duration-base:.16s` and `--duration-base:0s` present in compiled CSS. Does not trip the `prefers-color-scheme` acceptance check (different media feature).
- **Committed in:** `3e1188a`

**3. [Rule 1 — Bug] Outline Button's edge was on the decorative rule token**
- **Found during:** Task 1 (step 5)
- **Issue:** `outline` used `border-border`. After the swap that resolves to `--cena-rule`, which is **1.29:1** and WCAG 1.4.11-exempt *only because it is decorative*. An outline button's edge is a control boundary and carries the 3:1 non-text threshold — so the re-skin would have silently put a shipped control's only visual boundary below the accessibility floor while looking tidier.
- **Fix:** `border-input` (`--cena-border-control`, 3.55:1 on paper). Removed the now-redundant `dark:border-input`.
- **Files modified:** `components/ui/button.tsx`
- **Verification:** Reasoned against the UI-SPEC sweep (rows 14, 15); full suite green.
- **Committed in:** `3e1188a`

**4. [Rule 1 — Bug] Own comment tripped the new source scan**
- **Found during:** Task 2
- **Issue:** The `app/layout.tsx` comment explaining the `tokens/fonts.css` ban wrote the Google Fonts URL out literally, split across two lines. The new scan (which deliberately does not except comments) matched `url('https://fonts.` as a CSS `url()` asset position.
- **Fix:** Reworded to describe the URL rather than reproduce it, with an inline note explaining why.
- **Files modified:** `app/layout.tsx`
- **Verification:** `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` green; the allowlist still holds exactly one entry.
- **Committed in:** `2bb0b7a`

**Total deviations:** 4 auto-fixed (2 missing-critical, 2 bugs)
**Impact on plan:** All four are correctness or accessibility fixes inside the plan's own files. No scope creep; no architectural change; no Rule 4 escalation needed.

## Surfaced, Not Silently Resolved

The plan asked that judgement calls not covered by the (unsigned) UI-SPEC be surfaced rather than decided quietly.

- **Focus-ring alpha.** The plan says "keep the focus treatment as a 3px `--cena-accent` ring at **30%** alpha" and then says the existing `focus-visible:ring-ring/50` already expresses it. Those disagree — `/50` is 50%. The verb is *keep*, and the other 18 primitives (owned by other plans) all use `/50`, so changing it here alone would ship two focus treatments. **Left at `/50`.** If 30% is the intended contract, it is a one-line change that should land across all 19 primitives in the wave-3 re-skin, not here.
- **`01.1-UI-SPEC.md` remains unsigned** — `## Checker Sign-Off` has all six boxes unchecked and reads `**Approval:** pending`. This plan consumed its Color, Typography and Spacing sections verbatim. A later sign-off that changes a colour, a type role or a control height lands as rework here first. Wave 2 was the cheapest place for that exposure, as planned.

| Stub | File | Why intentional | Resolved by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.dark` overrides nothing | `app/tokens/cena.css` | The design project's dark token set was not retrievable (no `DesignSync` tool available — RESEARCH A2/A3/A14 stay open). No dark hex was invented: `--cena-accent #0B5FA5` on a tisza-900 dark paper computes **2.36:1**, so a naive polarity flip would ship a sub-AA set that looks plausible. This is threat **T-01.1-25**, mitigated by *not* authoring it. D-10 wires no dark UI in 01.1, so nothing regresses — dark currently resolves identically to light rather than to a half-migrated palette. | Theming milestone. Plan **01.1-06** must add the dark core pairs to the contrast sweep before any dark surface is wired. |

## Issues Encountered

- **Step 0's ramp fetch could not run.** No `DesignSync` tool is available to this executor, so `tokens/colors.css`, `tokens/spacing.css` and `tokens/semantic.css` were not fetched and RESEARCH assumptions **A2, A3 and A14 remain unresolved**. Proceeded with the locked UI-SPEC ramp as the plan directs. No threshold was weakened and no value was substituted — if a later fetch returns different values, the contrast sweep is the arbiter, not the source document.
- **`.design-sync/` preview bundle is now stale** (RESEARCH Pitfall 8, which predicted exactly this). `.design-sync/fonts/` holds Inter harvested from `.next/static/media`, and `.design-sync/tailwind-entry.css` *defines* `--font-sans` for the out-of-Next preview context; neither follows a font change, so previews will render in a browser-default face with nothing failing. Its `@source inline(...)` safelist also enumerates the token vocabulary and will not carry the new tokens. **Out of scope** — `.design-sync/*` is not in this plan's `files_modified` and touching it would be scope creep. Recorded in `.planning/WINDOWS.md` (entry 5); owed before the next design-sync capture.

## User Setup Required

None — no external service configuration required. (`next/font/google` needs network access to `fonts.gstatic.com` **at build time only**; it is cached in `.next/cache/fonts` and nothing reaches Google from the browser at runtime.)

## Next Phase Readiness

**Ready.** The pattern every later re-skin copies is established and proven:

- **For the primitive waves (01.1-07, 01.1-08):** `components/ui/button.tsx` is the worked example — semantic classes only, no raw hex, `min-h-11` for controls, and `tests/theme/touch-targets.test.ts` is built to be extended with more primitives by adding a source reader, not by rewriting the mechanism.
- **For 01.1-06 (venue namespace + contrast sweep):** `app/tokens/venue.css` slots into the same import block. Both existing token files are `:root`-only by design, leaving `@theme inline` free for the venue-themable tokens that require it. The dark ramp is owed to that plan's sweep once retrievable.
- **For the surface waves:** nothing needs a class rewrite — surfaces inherit the ramp through the semantic roles. The login page proved this by changing appearance without being edited.

**Carry forward:** the `.design-sync` staleness and the focus-ring alpha question are the two open threads; both are recorded above and neither blocks a subsequent plan.
